## Partnership Strategy – Helping Emerging‑Market Steel & Aluminium Suppliers Meet the EU CBAM (2026‑) **Goal:** Keep the EU buyer’s supply base intact, improve the carbon‑performance of Indian, Turkish and North‑African (Morocco‑Algeria‑Tunisia‑Egypt) partners, and turn the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) from a “threat” into a **joint value‑creation platform**. --- ### 1. Situation Snapshot | Dimension | What the EU buyer sees | What the suppliers see | Technical readiness | |-----------|------------------------|------------------------|----------------------| | **Regulatory** | CBAM will impose a carbon‑price at the EU border (based on verified embedded emissions). | Some view it as “green protectionism” – a hidden tariff that favours EU producers. | **India:** 30 % of large steel/aluminium firms have ISO‑14064‑1, internal carbon‑footprinting, but data granularity is low.
**Turkey:** 50 % have basic Scope 1‑2 reporting; limited Scope 3.
**North‑Africa:** 20 % have any formal carbon accounting; most rely on external consultants. | | **Commercial** | Need reliable, CBAM‑compliant volumes at cost‑competitive prices. | Fear of price erosion, “double‑taxation”, and loss of market share if they can’t absorb the carbon cost. | **Varied** – from mature integrated mills (high) to small‑scale smelters (low). | | **Strategic** | Preserve a diversified, resilient supply chain and meet EU ESG commitments. | Preserve export revenues, protect domestic competitiveness, and avoid being “punished” for global market forces. | **Low‑medium** for most SMEs, high for a few Tier‑1 integrators. | --- ### 2. Guiding Principles | # | Principle | Rationale | |---|-----------|-----------| | **1. Mutual Risk‑Sharing** | Costs of compliance are split (technical aid, financing, carbon‑price hedging). | Neutralises the “protectionism” narrative – the buyer is a partner, not a regulator. | | **2. Tiered Support Aligned to Readiness** | Three “Readiness Buckets” (High‑, Medium‑, Low‑) receive a tailored mix of services. | Efficient allocation of limited resources; avoids one‑size‑fits‑all. | | **3. Transparency & Co‑Governance** | Joint steering committee, open data‑exchange standards, third‑party verification. | Builds trust, demonstrates fairness, and satisfies CBAM verification requirements. | | **4. Shared Value Creation** | Decarbonisation projects are co‑invested, generating carbon‑credits that can be used to offset the buyer’s CBAM exposure. | Turns compliance cost into an asset that benefits both sides. | | **5. Local Legitimacy** | Engage national industry associations, ministries, and climate funds. | Reduces perception of “EU‑imposed protectionism” and taps existing financing instruments. | --- ### 3. Partnership Model – “CBAM Co‑Compliance Hub (CCH)” A **multi‑layered ecosystem** that brings together the EU buyer, suppliers, technology/financing partners, and verification bodies under a single digital and contractual framework. ``` ┌─────────────────────┐ │ EU Buyer (Lead) │ └─────────┬───────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────▼─────────────────────┐ │ CBAM Co‑Compliance Hub (CCH) │ │ (Legal entity – joint venture or 2026‑2027 │ │ “Partnership Agreement”) │ └───────┬───────────────┬───────────────┬─────┘ │ │ │ ┌───────▼───────┐ ┌─────▼─────┐ ┌───────▼───────┐ │ Technical │ │ Financial│ │ Verification │ │ Services │ │ Services │ │ Services │ └───────┬───────┘ └─────┬─────┘ └───────┬───────┘ │ │ │ ┌───────▼─────┐ ┌───────▼─────┐ ┌───────▼─────┐ │ Suppliers│ │ Banks / │ │ NGOs / │ │ (India, │ │ Funds │ │ Auditors │ │ Turkey, │ │ (green, │ │ (DNV, │ │ N‑Africa) │ │ climate) │ │ Carbon │ └────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ ``` | Layer | Core Deliverables | |------|-------------------| | **Legal/Contractual** | • 5‑year “Co‑Compliance Agreement” with clear cost‑share formulas (e.g., 60 % buyer, 40 % supplier).
•  Escrow‑account for carbon‑price hedging (EUAs, VERs). | | **Technical Services** | • On‑site carbon‑footprint audits (ISO‑14064, GHG Protocol).
• Digital carbon‑accounting platform (cloud‑based, API‑enabled for EU buyer’s CBAM reporting).
• Process‑optimisation pilots (e.g., electric‑arc furnace conversion, scrap‑increase, low‑carbon aluminium (bauxite‑free) routes). | | **Financial Services** | • Low‑interest “green‑working‑capital” lines (European Investment Bank, IDB, KfW).
• Carbon‑price risk‑hedge instruments (EU‑ETS futures, synthetic “CBAM forwards”).
• Grants for capital‑intensive upgrades (EAF, renewable electricity contracts). | | **Verification Services** | • Independent third‑party verification for each shipment (scope‑1/2 data).
• Joint audit schedule (quarterly) → EU‑acceptable CBAM certificates. | | **Market Access Services** | • Preferential contract terms for compliant shipments (price premium, longer contract horizon).
• Co‑branding “CBAM‑Compliant” label for downstream EU customers (boosts supplier reputation). | --- ### 4. Tiered Supplier Support Packages | Tier | Supplier Profile | Support Bundle (What the buyer contributes) | Expected Outcome (12‑24 mo) | |------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | **A – High‑Readiness** (e.g., Tata Steel, Hürriyet‑Demir, Arcelor‑Mittal‑Algeria) | • Established carbon accounting, Scope 1‑2 data, some renewable electricity. | • **Carbon‑price hedge** (EU‑ETS forward contracts) covering 80 % of estimated CBAM cost.
• **Co‑investment** in modest efficiency upgrades (e.g., waste‑heat recovery).
• **Joint marketing** of CBAM‑verified products. | • 100 % CBAM‑compliant shipments.
• 5‑10 % cost‑of‑goods reduction via waste‑heat/energy savings. | | **B – Medium‑Readiness** (mid‑size mills in Gujarat, Bursa, Tunisia) | • Basic GHG reporting, limited internal expertise, interested in finance. | • **Technical‑assistance package:** 4‑day on‑site carbon audit + remote data‑integration toolkit.
• **Financing bridge:** 5‑yr subsidised loan (2‑% interest) for process retrofit (e.g., 10 % EAF conversion).
• **Carbon‑credit sharing:** Supplier receives 30 % of any VERs generated from the retrofit. | • Reach 80 % verified emissions data.
• Reduce unit‑level embedded carbon by 15‑20 %. | | **C – Low‑Readiness** (small foundries, Algiers‑based aluminium workshops) | • No formal GHG data, rely on fossil‑fuel power, limited cash flow. | • **Capacity‑building hub:** 8‑week “Carbon Fundamentals” blended learning (local language, AR‑lab).
• **Zero‑up‑front‑cost upgrade:** Vendor‑financed energy‑efficiency kit (e.g., high‑efficiency burners) amortised via a “carbon‑savings surcharge” paid by the buyer.
• **Pilot **green‑electricity procurement** via PPA with regional solar farms – cost‑neutral after 3 years. | • First‑time GHG reporting (Scope 1‑2).
• Achieve CBAM‑eligible status for at least 30 % of output. | > **Key Point:** The buyer **funds up‑front** (technical, financing, risk‑hedge) while the supplier repays through **price‑linked carbon‑savings sharing**. This creates a *pay‑as‑you‑save* model that neutralises perceived unfairness. --- ### 5. Step‑by‑Step Implementation Road‑Map | Quarter | Milestone | Owner | Deliverables | |--------|-----------|-------|--------------| | **Q1‑2025** | **Foundational Set‑Up** | EU Buyer Legal & Procurement | • Sign “Co‑Compliance Framework” with three regional lead suppliers.
• Create CCH legal entity (in EU, with an office in Dubai for North‑Africa). | | **Q2‑2025** | **Carbon‑Accounting Platform Roll‑out** | CCH‑Tech Lead | • Deploy cloud‑based GHG data capture (ISO‑14064) → API to EU buyer’s CBAM portal.
• Conduct pilot audit at one Tier‑A & one Tier‑B supplier (India, Turkey). | | **Q3‑2025** | **Financing Instruments Launch** | CCH‑Finance Lead (EIB & local development banks) | • Issue first “CBAM‑Hedging Note” (EUR 10 M).
• Open green‑working‑capital line for Tier‑B/‑C partners. | | **Q4‑2025** | **Capacity‑Building Programme** | CCH‑Learning Lead | • Deliver 12 regional “Carbon Fundamentals” cohorts (local language, blended).
• Certify 150 mid‑level engineers as “CBAM‑Compliant Operators”. | | **Q1‑2026** | **First CBAM‑Verified Shipments** | Procurement & Supplier Ops | • Submit verified carbon‑price statements for 3 % of total EU‑buyer steel/aluminium volume (pilot). | | **Q2‑2026** | **Market‑Access Incentive** | Commercial & Marketing | • Introduce “CBAM‑Preferred Supplier” pricing tier (2 % premium) for compliant shipments. | | **Q3‑2026** | **Policy Dialogue & Advocacy** | EU Buyer + Supplier Associations | • Co‑host EU‑India/​Turkey/​North‑Africa round‑table on CBAM fairness; push for WTO‑compatible border‑adjustment rules. | | **Q4‑2026** | **Scale‑Up & Review** | CCH Steering Committee | • Review KPIs (see Section 7).
• Adjust cost‑share ratios for next 5‑year cycle. | --- ### 6. Governance & Decision‑Making | Body | Composition | Mandate | Meeting Cadence | |------|--------------|---------|-----------------| | **CCH Steering Committee** | CEO of EU buyer, 1 senior exec from each supplier country, 2 independent ESG experts, 1 EU Commission liaison. | Strategic direction, budget approval, dispute resolution. | Quarterly (plus ad‑hoc for major issues). | | **Technical Advisory Board (TAB)** | 3 carbon‑accounting firms, 2 universities (one in each region), 1 supplier R&D head. | Methodology standards, data‑quality audit, technology scouting. | Bi‑monthly. | | **Finance & Risk Committee** | Representatives from EIB, local development banks, buyer’s treasury, supplier CFOs. | Design of hedging, loan terms, cost‑share formulas. | Monthly. | | **Verification Council** | Accredited auditors (DNV, SGS, TÜV), supplier internal auditors, buyer’s compliance. | Approve CBAM certificates, oversee third‑party verification schedule. | Quarterly. | All minutes, decisions and KPI dashboards are uploaded to a **shared governance portal** (access‑controlled, multilingual) to guarantee transparency. --- ### 7. Success Metrics (KPIs) | KPI | Target (End‑2026) | How Measured | |-----|-------------------|--------------| | **% of total volume CBAM‑verified** | ≥ 70 % (EU buyer total spend) | CCH carbon‑accounting platform + verification certificates. | | **Average embedded CO₂ intensity reduction** | 15 % vs. 2024 baseline (tier‑weighted) | GHG inventory per supplier. | | **Carbon‑price exposure covered by hedge** | 80 % of estimated CBAM cost for Tier‑A/B | Hedging contracts in escrow. | | **Supplier financing uptake** | €200 M of green‑working‑capital deployed | Finance‑committee reports. | | **Training completion** | 90 % of identified mid‑level staff certified | Learning‑management system. | | **Perceived fairness (survey)** | ≥ 70 % favorable rating among suppliers | Annual pulse survey (anonymous). | | **Joint‑value creation (revenue uplift)** | €50 M incremental premium revenue from “CBAM‑Preferred” label. | Commercial reporting. | --- ### 8. Managing the “Protectionism” Narrative | Action | Rationale | Execution | |--------|-----------|-----------| | **Co‑ownership of Costs** | Shows the buyer is **not** imposing a unilateral surcharge. | Cost‑share formulas baked into contracts, disclosed publicly. | | **Joint Advocacy** | Suppliers become **allies** in a WTO‑compatible dialogue, turning them from opponents to co‑advocates. | Sponsor a trilateral EU‑India‑Turkey‑North‑Africa industry forum (annual). | | **Benefit‑Sharing of Carbon Credits** | Any VERs or EUA surplus generated are **shared** (e.g., 30 % to supplier, 70 % to buyer). | Set up a “Carbon‑Credit Pool” managed by CCH. | | **Transparency Portal** | Real‑time visibility of CBAM calculations, audits, and hedging costs removes suspicion. | Deploy a web dashboard (multi‑language, GDPR‑compliant). | | **Local Champions** | Identify respected industry leaders (e.g., Indian Steel Association President) to publicly endorse the partnership. | Provide them with data packs, speaking opportunities at EU events. | --- ### 9. Funding Sources & Instruments | Source | Instrument | Typical Size | Conditions | |--------|------------|--------------|------------| | **European Investment Bank (EIB)** | Green‑Project Loans (≤ 5 yr, 2‑% interest) | €50‑150 M per country | Demonstrated emissions reduction ≥ 10 %. | | **European Union Horizon‑Europe / Innovation Fund** | Grant for low‑carbon technology pilots (e.g., hydrogen‑based reduction). | €5‑20 M per pilot | Must include EU‑buyer as co‑applicant. | | **International Development Bank (IDB)** | Sustainable Working‑Capital Facility | €30‑80 M total | Focus on North‑African SMEs. | | **Private Climate Funds (e.g., ClimateInvest) ** | Equity‑style “green‑upgrade” investment (10‑30 % stake). | €10‑40 M per plant | Exit after 5‑7 years via buy‑back from EU buyer. | | **Carbon‑Market Hedge** | Forward contracts on EU‑ETS allowances (€/tCO₂) | Up to €100 M notional | Counter‑party risk managed via EU‑cleared exchange. | | **Supplier‑Side “Carbon‑Savings Surcharge”** | A small surcharge (≈ €0.3/tCO₂) on each invoice, earmarked for upgrades. | Variable | Transparent ledger, refundable if emissions targets overshoot. | All financing is **channeled through the CCH**, enabling a single point of contact for suppliers and simplifying due‑diligence. --- ### 10. Risk Management | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | |------|------------|--------|------------| | **Regulatory drift** – CBAM rules change after 2026. | Medium | High (investment stranded) | Continuous legal monitoring; include a “regulatory‑adaptation clause” allowing contract renegotiation. | | **Supplier default** on financing. | Low‑Medium (Tier‑C) | Medium | Structured “pay‑as‑you‑save” repayment; cash‑flow linked to shipment milestones. | | **Data‑quality disputes** (different accounting methods). | Medium | High (certificate rejections) | Adopt **GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard** + third‑party verification; create a “Data‑Reconciliation Working Group”. | | **Perceived unfairness → contract termination**. | Low‑Medium | High | Embed **fair‑play clauses**: early‑termination penalties capped; offer “exit‑to‑market” option with a transition period. | | **Currency volatility** (₹, TRY, DZD, EGP). | Medium | Medium | Hedging via FX forwards; financing denominated in Euro with local conversion facilities. | | **Technology lock‑in** (single supplier of retrofit kits). | Low | Medium | Establish **open‑procurement** for technology upgrades; maintain a preferred‑vendor list. | --- ### 11. Communication Blueprint | Audience | Core Message | Channel | Frequency | |----------|--------------|---------|-----------| | **Senior EU Buyer** | “Our supply chain is future‑proof, compliant, and cost‑neutral.” | Executive briefing, ESG report, Board update | Quarterly | | **Supplier CEOs** | “You keep market access – we share the compliance cost and the upside of carbon‑credits.” | One‑to‑one virtual meetings, joint press release | Bi‑monthly | | **Shop‑floor Engineers** | “New tools will lower fuel use, make work safer, and bring a bonus when emissions drop.” | On‑site workshops, AR‑guided tutorials, local language newsletters | Monthly | | **Local Industry Associations** | “We’re co‑designing a WTO‑compatible solution; your members will stay competitive.” | Regional round‑tables, webinars, policy briefs | Quarterly | | **Public / NGOs** | “Transparent partnership protecting jobs while cutting carbon.” | Dedicated “CBAM‑Partner” microsite, social media, sustainability reports | Ongoing | | **EU Regulators** | “We meet CBAM verification standards and support developing‑country industry.” | Formal compliance submissions, audit reports | As required (per CBAM timeline) | All external messages are **pre‑tested** with a “Cultural‑Fit Review Panel” (local experts in India, Turkey, Morocco, Egypt) to ensure tone, metaphors, and claims resonate. --- ### 12. Example Pilot – **Hyderabad Steelworks (India)** | Aspect | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Readiness** | Tier‑B (medium). Has ISO‑14064‑1, uses coal‑based blast furnace. | | **Technical Package** | • 4‑day onsite GHG audit (DNV).
• Installation of a low‑cost waste‑heat recovery system (US $2 M). | | **Financing** | • €5 M green loan from EIB (2 % interest, 5‑yr).
• EU‑ETS forward hedge covering 80 % of projected CBAM cost. | | **Carbon‑Credit Sharing** | Expected VER generation = 150 kt CO₂e (2027‑2030) → 30 % to Hyderabad, 70 % to buyer (used to offset buyer’s own CBAM exposure). | | **Commercial Outcome** | • 12 % reduction in embedded CO₂ per tonne of steel.
• Buyer grants a 2 % price premium for 3 years. | | **Fairness Signal** | Public joint press‑release: “Partnered to keep Indian steel competitive in Europe.” | The pilot can be **replicated** across 2‑3 other Tier‑B firms by Q3‑2026. --- ### 13. Summary – How the Strategy Turns Tension into Competitive Advantage 1. **Cost‑Sharing & Hedging** neutralises the perception that CBAM is a hidden tariff. 2. **Tiered, capacity‑building support** brings low‑readiness suppliers up to speed without imposing unrealistic expectations. 3. **Joint ownership of carbon‑credits** creates a new revenue stream that benefits **both** sides. 4. **Transparent digital platform + third‑party verification** satisfies EU regulators and builds supplier confidence. 5. **Policy advocacy and co‑branding** reposition the partnership from “EU‑imposed” to “global‑value‑creation”. By the end of 2026, the EU buyer will have **secured a compliant, resilient supply chain**; the Indian, Turkish and North‑African partners will have **reduced emissions, accessed cheap financing, and kept their EU market share**—all while feeling that the CBAM regime is a **shared challenge, not a punitive barrier**.
